items.bold: US blockade REMAINS "in full force" — Trump: negotiations will go very quickly.
items.text: Trump hailed the Hormuz opening and thanked Tehran, but stated the US blockade of Iranian ports "will remain in full force" until the two sides reach a peace deal. items.bold: Iran DEPUTY FM: Seeking comprehensive end to war, not just temporary extension.

items.bold: US HOUSE war powers resolution narrowly failed 213-214.
items.text: House war powers resolution to limit Trump's Iran military actions narrowly failed 213-214. Rep. Warren Davidson (R-Ohio) voted present rather than yes or no — the key swing vote. Rep. Thomas Massie (R-Kentucky) was the only Republican to vote in favour. Rep. Jared Golden (D-Maine) was the only Democrat to vote against. Senate had also failed to advance similar measure Wednesday. Trump retains full executive authority to continue military operations. Fourth consecutive failure in Congress to limit war powers.

military.t: HORMUZ DECLARED COMPLETELY OPEN — Iran FM Araghchi Official Statement
military.d: Iranian FM Abbas Araghchi posted on social media Friday: "In line with the ceasefire in Lebanon, the passage for all commercial vessels through Strait of Hormuz is declared completely open for the remaining period of ceasefire, on the coordinated route as already announced by Ports and Maritime Organisation of the Islamic Republic of Iran." This is the single most significant development since the war began February 28. Dow Futures immediately rallied 500+ points. For India: LPG tankers, crude carriers, all commercial ships free to transit. 20,000 seafarers stuck since February 28 can now move. 230+ loaded oil tankers in Gulf can exit. India's energy import crisis is materially easing — CONDITIONALLY on ceasefire holding.

military.t: US Blockade of Iranian Ports REMAINS — Trump: "Negotiations Go Very Quickly"
military.d: Trump hailed Iran's Hormuz opening and thanked Tehran, but stated clearly the US blockade of Iranian ports "will remain in full force" until the two sides reach a formal peace deal. Trump: "Negotiations should go very quickly." This means the US has achieved what it wanted — commercial shipping freed — while maintaining economic pressure on Iran to sign final deal. Two-track pressure continues: open strait + blocked Iranian ports. Watch for second round Islamabad talks confirmation this weekend as next key trigger.

military.t: House War Powers Resolution Failed 213-214 — Trump Retains Full Authority
military.d: Republican-led House narrowly failed to adopt war powers resolution 213-214. Rep. Warren Davidson (R-Ohio) voted present — the critical swing vote. Rep. Thomas Massie (R-Kentucky) only Republican in favour. Rep. Jared Golden (D-Maine) only Democrat against. Senate had similarly blocked measure Wednesday. Trump retains full executive authority. Fourth consecutive Congressional failure to limit war powers. War powers debate will continue but no legislative constraint on Trump actions.

military.t: Iran Deputy FM: Seeking Comprehensive End, Not Just Temporary Extension
military.d: Iran's deputy foreign minister stated Tehran rejects any purely temporary ceasefire and is seeking a comprehensive end to the war across all fronts — Iran, Lebanon, Gaza, Iraq. Iran Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf: approaching Lebanon ceasefire "cautiously," will remain until "complete victory achieved." Mohsen Rezaei hardline framing: ceasefire was "imposed on Zionist-American adversary" by Hezbollah resistance. Iran domestically framing Hormuz opening and Lebanon ceasefire as victories not concessions — critical for deal to be politically sellable in Tehran. This is why Iranian deputy FM language is important — sets the frame for second round talks.

military.t: South Korea: First Crude Tanker Via Red Sea Since Hormuz Closed
military.d: South Korean government confirmed a vessel transported crude oil through the Red Sea for the first time since the Strait of Hormuz was effectively closed when the war began. Ship loaded crude at Saudi Arabia's Yanbu port and safely exited via alternative route to South Korea. Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries confirmed. President Lee Jae Myung called it a "valuable achievement." First tangible sign of shipping normalization via alternative routes. India similarly using Red Sea-Suez alternative for some routes. Full Hormuz normalization still weeks away due to mine clearance.

military.t: Mines Still in Hormuz — UK-France Summit on Minesweeping
military.d: Despite Hormuz being declared open, significant mine risk remains. NBC: "not immediately clear what it would mean for concerns about mines." Earlier reports: Iran lost track of mines it planted, unable to fully clear the route. US minesweeping operations ongoing. UK-France virtual summit held to discuss ways to restore shipping given mine threat. For India: war-risk insurance premiums will remain elevated until mines certified cleared. Freight operators and P&I clubs will take time to reclassify Hormuz as standard transit zone. Full shipping cost normalisation likely 3-6 months.

military.d: With Hormuz declared completely open, India's 8 LPG carriers and crude tankers in the Gulf can transit freely. 280 Indian seafarers can move. Operation Urja Suraksha remains on standby. For household impact: if Brent falls below $85 as supply normalises (Choice Equity: Brent averaging $95 Apr-Jun then $82 Jul-Sep), LPG price cut possible within 2-3 weeks of sustained opening. military.d: Israel-Lebanon 10-day ceasefire appears to be holding. Tens of thousands of displaced Lebanese rushing back toward southern Lebanon despite official warnings. Lebanese President Aoun called negotiations with Israel "delicate and crucial." Israel Defence Minister Katz: invasion "has not yet been completed" — keeping troops in south. Netanyahu rejected Hezbollah disarmament demands. US hopes ceasefire eventually leads to permanent peace agreement. Lebanon deaths: 2,196 confirmed by National News Agency as of Apr 17. assessment.body:
Day 49 close is the most important evening since the war began on February 28.

THE HORMUZ OPENING — WHAT IT MEANS FOR INDIA
• Iran FM Araghchi, official post: "passage for ALL commercial vessels declared completely open"
• All commercial shipping — India LPG tankers, crude carriers, container ships — can transit
• 20,000 seafarers stuck since February 28 can now move
• 230+ loaded oil tankers in the Gulf waiting to exit can now do so
• India energy import crisis materially easing — CONDITIONALLY on ceasefire holding
• LPG price cut possible in 2-3 weeks if Brent falls below Rs 85
• Petrol/diesel hike risk removed
• Fertiliser supply for kharif sowing season resuming
• Cooking oil, medicine API supply chains normalising

THE IMPORTANT CAVEATS
• US blockade of Iranian PORTS remains "in full force" until peace deal
• Mines still in Hormuz — UK-France minesweeping summit underway
• Iran lost track of some mines — US minesweeping ongoing
• War-risk insurance and P&I clubs will take weeks to reclassify Hormuz
• Full shipping cost normalisation likely 3-6 months (Choice Equity)
• Iran deputy FM: seeking comprehensive deal, not temporary extension
• Hormuz opening tied explicitly to Lebanon ceasefire — if Lebanon ceasefire breaks, Hormuz could close again

INDIA MARKETS — CLOSE AND WEEK SUMMARY
• Sensex Apr 17 close: 78,494 (+505 / +0.65%)
• Nifty Apr 17 close: 24,354 (+157 / +0.65%)
• Sensex now just 205 points from pre-war 78,699 — almost fully erased war losses
• Week performance: recovered from 76,847 (Apr 13) to 78,494 = +1,647 pts in 3 trading sessions
• FII net buyers Rs 382 Cr Apr 16 — structural positive turn
• India VIX falling to near pre-war levels
• Next week: Infosys results April 23 — major IT bellwether

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT
• Second round Islamabad talks expected this weekend
• Peace deal framework by April 22 (ceasefire expiry) the target
• If deal confirmed: Brent to $72-80, Sensex 82,000-88,000, rupee to 90-91
• India direct benefit: LPG cut, petrol/diesel cut, rupee appreciation, FII return
• If ceasefire extends without full deal: Brent $80-88, Sensex 80,000-82,000
• If Lebanon ceasefire breaks and Iran closes Hormuz again: Brent $110-120, sharp reversal

VERDICT: February 28 was the worst day for India's energy security in a generation. April 17 may be the day it turned. Hormuz is open. Lebanon ceasefire is holding. Pakistan has built a deal framework. The question now is whether the second round of talks in Islamabad can convert all of this into a signed agreement before April 22. India is 5 days from the biggest energy security relief since the war began.
